builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Scaling Influence Functions in LLMs through Eigenbasis-Corrected One-Bit Gradient Projection
summary: EOGP replaces storing full or low-rank per-example training gradients for influence-function queries with an EK-FAC subspace projection, PCA-learned compression directions, and one-bit quantized coordinates. The cost is a preprocessing pass computing EK-FAC statistics and PCA over training gradients, plus implementation complexity, and influence estimates remain approximations whose accuracy depends on how well the retained subspace covers future unknown queries. It can fail when query gradients lie outside the retained eigenbasis, when EK-FAC's Kronecker-factor assumptions poorly match the model's curvature, or when one-bit quantization error dominates for examples with atypical gradient directions.
rationale: Influence-based data attribution is a specialized diagnostic workflow rather than a production inference need, and the method requires full training-gradient access and nontrivial EK-FAC infrastructure, so the reader should adopt it only if data-attribution analysis becomes an actual requirement.
technique: One-bit compressed gradients for influence functions

claims.statement: EOGP replaces storing full or low-rank per-example training gradients for influence-function queries with an EK-FAC subspace projection, PCA-learned compression directions, and one-bit quantized coordinates. The cost is a preprocessing pass computing EK-FAC statistics and PCA over training gradients, plus implementation complexity, and influence estimates remain approximations whose accuracy depends on how well the retained subspace covers future unknown queries. It can fail when query gradients lie outside the retained eigenbasis, when EK-FAC's Kronecker-factor assumptions poorly match the model's curvature, or when one-bit quantization error dominates for examples with atypical gradient directions.

On GPT-2, EOGP predicts retraining outcomes more accurately than compression baselines at one-sixteenth of their per-example storage; on OLMo 2 SFT models (1B-32B) it remains competitive with baselines given over 100x the storage.
